newsitem.title: USA: Long terms for Los Angeles' "wrong-turn murder".
newsitem.headline: Long terms for Los Angeles' "wrong-turn murder".

text.p: Three suspected gang members were sentenced on Friday to 54 years to life for the murder of a toddler in a car that was riddled with bullets after making a wrong turn into a dark dead-end street.

The killing of 2-year-old Stephanie Kuhen on Sept. 17, 1995, grabbed national attention and was cited by President Bill Clinton during his re-election campaign as an example of street violence plaguing the country.
As the three men were sentenced by Superior Court Judge Edward Ferns, the little girl's grandmother aimed a tirade at the convicted killers.
"How dare you!" Linda Dalton screamed. "You're no better than wild animals, and I want you to be locked in a cage forever so you can never hurt another family like mine."

The girl was returning from a picnic with her mother, uncle and two brothers in a car driven by a family friend late at night. The car took a wrong turn into an unlighted dead-end street in a gang-infested area of Los Angeles.
When the driver tried to back out of the street, several young men blocked its exit with trash cans and opened fire.
Stephanie was hit in the head and killed. A brother was wounded in the foot, and the driver was wounded in the back.
Three of the five people arrested for the killing were sentenced for murder on Friday: Anthony Rodriguez, 28; Hugo Gomez, 17, and Manuel Rosales, 23.

Augustin Lizama, 17, who investigators said put trash cans in front of the car, faces a retrial because jurors were deadlocked on the charges against him. Marcos Luna, 25, pleaded guilty earlier to an assault charge and was sent to prison.
Gomez was the only defendant to address the court on Friday. "I'm an Avenues gang member, I admit it. But I did not murder Stephanie Kuhen. I want to say I'm sorry for what happened," he said.
In a pre-sentencing report read in court, probation officer Will Manson wrote that when he was arrested, Gomez said, "The only reason that this is a big deal is because it was a ... white kid."
